To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

progesterone and γ-aminobutiric acid receptor agonists stimulate oscillatory calcium signals, ciliary beat frequency, and the association of GABA receptor subunits in the mouse oocyte transport epithelium.

P4 and GABAB receptor agonists stimulate cilia in oviduct cells through activation of the nonselective Ca2+-permeable TRPV4 channel and GABAA receptors, which are physically associated with GABAB receptors.
progesterone and γ-aminobutiric acid receptor agonists stimulate the ciliary beat of mouse oviduct cells by coupling to the cationic TRPV4 channel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of rapid progesterone action in the oviducal cilia and the transport of oocytes and embryos.
the functional coupling of GABAB receptors and the channel protein TRPV4 in the rapid modulation of ciliary beat frequency by progesterone and agonists of GABAA receptors.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the transport of oocytes and embryos along the ciliated oviducal epithelium, a process in which P4 is thought to be a key regulator of ciliary activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
P4 and GABAA/B receptor agonists stimulate Ca2+-mediated CBF in the oviducal epithelium through a molecular mechanism in the cilia that involves TRPV4 and GABAB receptor–coupled Gi/o proteins.

P4, through its binding to GABARs, stimulates TRPV4-mediated cation influx, which is essential for the initiation and maintenance of the oscillatory Ca2+, and consequently, the acceleration of the cilial beat frequency.
P4 and GABAA/B receptor agonists rapidly activate TRPV4 and stimulate Ca2+ oscillatory activity and increased ciliary beating in the oviducal epithelium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
progesterone stimulates the cilia in the ovidut through the GABAergic signaling pathway.
progesterone and its agonist GABA stimulate the ciliary beat in mouse oviduct by a rapid signaling mechanism that requires the activation of GABA receptor subtypes A and B and the channel TRP4.

progesterone and γ-aminobutryic acid (GABA) receptor agonists stimulate the beating of oviductal cilia by activating the channel transient receptor potential vanilloid 4 (TRPV4) in close proximity of the inositol triphosphate receptor (IP3R) and G-protein–coupled GABA receptors (GABAA and GABA-B).
The main takeaway from our work is that
P4 and GABAA/B agonists rapidly stimulate cilial beating through the functional coupling of GABAB1, GABAA, and TRPV4 receptors.
progesterone and agonists of the γ-aminoburyric acid (GABA) receptor stimulate cilial beating by activating the cationic TRP channel 4 (TRPV4) in a stepwise manner.
progesterone and agonists of GABAA receptors stimulate TRPV4 channels in a stepwise process that requires GABAB receptors to accelerate ciliary beating.
